summary:
We develop this project with the ideas we have in our group of how to improve  the  monitroing health of the astronauts in the space , for this we use differents super inteligences, that help us programing the web , this website will help the astronauts to monitorate his levels of glucose constantly . also we use our knowlegge in robotics to build the hardware of the project. Implementing a continuous monitoring system will be highly useful for detecting anomalies that affect astronaut performance, as there are conditions such as nocturnal hypoglycemia that cause drops in blood glucose levels, which compromise the quality of rest and, consequently, their performance.For this reason, continuous glucose monitoring can be considered an essential system for tracking the health of astronauts.
Consequently, we decided to design a glucose measurement system intended to be scalable through improved ergonomics and the implementation of continuous data readings, complemented by a system for communicating with Earth via infrared light.

The entire system is designed to detect anomalies in glucose levels that could negatively affect the astronauts' rest and productivity.
details:
Technical operation of the experimental non-invasive glucometer prototype.

The project involves the development of an experimental prototype designed to investigate the non-invasive estimation of glucose by combining ultrasonic and optical signals, using an ESP32 DevKit V1 microcontroller as the processing unit.

The system primarily consists of an HC-SR04 ultrasonic module, a KY-039 optical sensor, and a reflective metal plate. The HC-SR04 generates ultrasonic bursts when its TRIG input is activated, while the metal plate is positioned on the opposite side of the finger to serve as a reflective surface. Simultaneously, the KY-039 sensor detects variations in light intensity linked to the optical properties of the tissue and pulsatile blood volume and converts them into analog electrical signals.

The ESP32 acquires these signals via its analog-to-digital converter, using a programmed sampling rate of approximately 333 samples per second. It then performs mathematical processing by identifying the maximum and minimum values ​​within each three-second acquisition window. From these values, it calculates the peak-to-peak amplitude, the average of the readings, and the corresponding voltage.

The results are transmitted wirelessly via the ESP32’s integrated Wi-Fi to a computer connected to the same local network. This communication utilizes the HTTP protocol and JSON format, while a server developed in Python using Flask receives the data and stores it in CSV files for subsequent analysis.

In this way, the prototype integrates signal acquisition, ultrasonic activation, digital processing, and wireless communication, providing an experimental platform to study the potential relationship between variations in the optical signal and blood glucose concentration. The results obtained represent experimental parameters of the optical signal and do not constitute clinical glucose measurements in mg/dL, until a quantitative relationship with reference measurements is demonstrated and validated.
